title: Grading and reporting
practice: Grade three sources and write one cited finding.

lessons.title: Source and information grading
lessons.intro: Grading says how far you trust a source (A to E) and its information (1 to 5), separately. A reliable source can still pass on something it heard second-hand.

tryit.prompt: Grade each item. Source: A always reliable to E untested. Information: 1 known to be true to 5 suspected false.
items: A bank's own statement of transactions
A neighbour's memory of a time
Something a friend says someone else told them

sandbox.task: Grade three items in the evidence viewer.

check.hint: Who said it, and what was said.

check.q: A reliable source passes on a rumour. The information grade is…
check.hint: Reliable people can repeat unreliable things.
They show how far to trust it.

lessons.title: Corroboration
lessons.intro: A point is stronger when independent sources agree. Two copies of the same record are one source, not two. Look for different kinds of evidence pointing the same way.

tryit.prompt: Which pair corroborates where the parcel was left?
options: Two copies of the same tracking export
Copies of one record are one source.
The delivery photo and a resident's public post
Right. Different sources, made independently, agree.
The driver's statement and the driver's tracking scan
Both come from the driver, so they are not independent.
Made separately and do not rely on each other
check.hint: Think about where each came from.

lessons.title: Writing a finding and building a cited report
lessons.intro: Good findings are short, specific and cited. A good report separates what is proved, what is likely and what is unknown, and says what should happen next.

options: Too vague, no citation, and it overclaims.
The delivery photo and GPS show the parcel was left at number 14, not 41 (EV-006).
Everything points to number 14 so it is definitely there now.
It overclaims: nobody has checked it is still there.

sandbox.task: Write the report summary and record a cited inference.

steps.label: Record an inference that cites evidence
Write a summary of at least 15 words

check.q: 'Definitely' in a conclusion that rests on inference is…
check.hint: Match the wording to the evidence.

check.q: What belongs in gaps and limitations?
options: What you could not prove or check
check.hint: Being honest about limits makes a report stronger.
